issues.label: Trial court jurisdiction proper
issues.why: Court must confirm statutory basis for jurisdiction under MCL 712A.2(b)(1) and (2) was supported and properly exercised.

issues.label: Validity of no-contest plea
issues.why: Court must ensure the plea was knowing/voluntary and had an adequate factual basis to support adjudication.

issues.label: Effect of ICWA removal
issues.why: Court must ensure the middle child’s ICWA-related removal does not affect procedures, findings, or standards applied to the remaining children.

issues.label: Preliminary removal findings
issues.why: Court must confirm required findings (contrary to welfare/necessity of removal/reasonable efforts or exceptions) were made at the preliminary stage.

issues.label: Reasonable efforts obligation
issues.why: Court must decide whether DHHS made reasonable efforts toward reunification given the “reasonable efforts” issue raised on appeal.

issues.label: Reasonable efforts scope/timing
issues.why: Court must assess whether efforts were reasonable throughout the case, including after new problems (meth use) were discovered.

issues.label: Service plan adequacy
issues.why: Court must determine whether the PATP was appropriately tailored to the barriers (medical neglect, SUD, mental health, parenting capacity, housing/income).

issues.label: Service plan amendments proper
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether adding SUD treatment/drug screens was justified, communicated, and implemented fairly.

issues.label: Access to evaluations/services
issues.why: Court must consider whether respondent had meaningful access to psychological evaluation, SUD treatment, parenting supports, transportation, and scheduling.

issues.label: DHHS follow-up and referrals
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether DHHS reasonably followed up after discharges and provided appropriate re-referrals/alternatives (e.g., inpatient) as recommended.

issues.label: Drug testing reliability/use
issues.why: Court must consider admissibility/weight of drug screen results and whether consistent positives support continued substance use.

issues.label: Mental health treatment efforts
issues.why: Court must assess whether recommended mental-health interventions were offered and whether respondent engaged/benefited.

issues.label: Inpatient treatment consideration
issues.why: Court must decide whether inpatient SUD treatment was reasonably pursued once evaluation recommended it and outpatient failed.

issues.label: Parenting-time facilitation
issues.why: Court must assess whether DHHS reasonably facilitated visitation and whether missed visits were attributable to respondent versus system barriers.

issues.label: Benefit from parenting education
issues.why: Court must determine whether completion of classes without demonstrated benefit supports statutory grounds and best-interest findings.

issues.label: Housing stability evaluation
issues.why: Court must resolve whether respondent had stable, suitable housing and whether DHHS’s concerns about the lease were materially justified.

issues.label: Income and ability to provide
issues.why: Court must consider whether lack of verifiable legal income affects ability to provide proper care and custody and whether assistance suffices.

issues.label: Medical neglect remediation
issues.why: Court must determine whether the conditions leading to adjudication (youngest child’s medical neglect/failure to thrive) were rectified or likely to be rectified.

issues.label: Compliance vs benefit standard
issues.why: Court must apply the correct legal standard—participation alone is insufficient without benefit—when evaluating progress on the PATP.

issues.label: Statutory ground identification
issues.why: Court must confirm the correct statutory ground relied upon (MCL 712A.19b(3)(c)(i)) despite the trial court’s generic reference to (c).

issues.label: Elements of 19b(3)(c)(i)
issues.why: Court must find (1) 182+ days since initial disposition, (2) conditions continue, and (3) no reasonable likelihood of rectification within a reasonable time.

issues.label: 182-day calculation
issues.why: Court must verify the timing from initial disposition to termination satisfies the 182-day requirement.

issues.label: Define “conditions” correctly
issues.why: Court must identify the relevant “conditions that led to adjudication” and any later-added barriers that are properly considered under (c)(i).

issues.label: Reasonable time for each child
issues.why: Court must assess “reasonable time” in light of each child’s age, needs, placement stability, and respondent’s progress.

issues.label: Clear and convincing evidence
issues.why: Court must ensure statutory grounds were proven by clear and convincing evidence.

issues.label: Due process and notice
issues.why: Court must ensure respondent had notice of allegations, service requirements, and potential termination, and a fair opportunity to participate.

issues.label: Evidentiary foundation
issues.why: Court must ensure critical findings (drug use, discharges, lack of benefit, housing instability) are supported by admissible evidence/record.

issues.label: Separate findings per child
issues.why: Court must consider whether grounds and best interests were evaluated for each child individually, not in a generalized manner.

issues.label: Oldest child not in foster care
issues.why: Court must consider how termination applies when the oldest child was placed with her biological father rather than in foster care.

issues.label: Father’s caregiver status effect
issues.why: Court must consider whether the oldest child’s biological father’s placement changes best-interest analysis and permanency planning.

issues.label: Best-interests preponderance
issues.why: Court must decide whether termination is in each child’s best interests by a preponderance of the evidence.

issues.label: Bond with mother
issues.why: Court must evaluate the strength/quality of the parent-child bond and whether it weighs against termination.

issues.label: Parenting ability and safety
issues.why: Court must assess respondent’s parenting capacity and the risk posed by ongoing meth use and unmet mental-health needs.

issues.label: Child’s need for permanence
issues.why: Court must weigh the children’s need for stability and permanency against the likelihood of reunification in a reasonable time.

issues.label: Placement advantages comparison
issues.why: Court must compare the benefits of current placements (licensed foster care; father’s care) versus returning to respondent.

issues.label: Sibling considerations
issues.why: Court must consider sibling relationships and any impact from differing placements/proceedings (including the ICWA-separated child) where relevant to best interests.

issues.label: Least restrictive/permanency options
issues.why: Court must consider whether alternatives to termination (guardianship, custody with father, extended time) are viable given the record.

issues.label: Impact of continued services
issues.why: Court must consider whether additional time/services would likely lead to rectification versus merely prolonging instability.

issues.label: Termination consequences for custody
issues.why: Court must account for how termination affects legal rights/decision-making, especially for the oldest child already living with her father.

issues.label: Adequacy of trial court findings
issues.why: Court must ensure the trial court made sufficiently specific factual findings and legal conclusions to permit appellate review.

issues.label: Preservation/standard of review
issues.why: Court must determine whether reasonable-efforts and other claims were preserved and apply the correct appellate standards (clear error, etc.).
